title: PCL sync uses fixed 5-second wait — no polling for completion
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx — handleSync() function

Root Cause: handleSync() calls complianceService.syncPCL(projectId) which enqueues a background job, then unconditionally waits 5 seconds via setTimeout before re-fetching the compliance map. The PCL sync job runs asynchronously and may take 15–30 seconds for large frameworks with many linked sources. The 5-second wait is an arbitrary constant that is rarely sufficient. There is no polling loop, no /pcl/status check, and no completion webhook.

Claude Fix Prompt: In FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx, replace the handleSync function's setTimeout(5000) approach with a polling loop that checks GET /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/pcl/status every 3 seconds until status changes from 'computing' to 'ready', 'stale', or 'failed' (max 10 attempts = 30 seconds). Show a progress indicator (spinner in the Sync PCL button) during polling. On completion, call loadData(). On timeout, show a toast "Sync is taking longer than expected — check back in a moment" and stop polling.
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — polling loop 3s×10 confirmed in handleSync() lines 654–679; setSyncing inside poll resolver

title: Licensing gate relies on stale `isLicensed` flag at page load
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworksManager.jsx — activation gate check; vibrantix-backend/src/modules/compliance-frameworks/client-frameworks.controller.js — addToProject()

Root Cause: The isLicensed field is set once when availableFrameworks is fetched at page load time by calling getLicensedFrameworkIds(orgId). If the org's subscription changes after page load (downgrade, trial expiry), the UI still shows isLicensed=true for frameworks that are no longer covered. The backend correctly re-checks licensing in addToProject, but when it returns a 403, the UI shows a generic error toast rather than a clear "subscription required" message, confusing the user.

Claude Fix Prompt:
1. In client-frameworks.controller.js addToProject(): When isFrameworkLicensed() returns false, return { error: 'LICENSING_REQUIRED', message: 'This framework requires an active subscription. Contact your org admin.' } with HTTP 403.
2. In FrameworksManager.jsx handleToggle(): In the catch block, check if err.response?.data?.error === 'LICENSING_REQUIRED' and show the subscription modal instead of a generic error toast. This ensures plan-change race conditions are handled gracefully.
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — backend 403 returns `{error:'LICENSING_REQUIRED'}` (controller line 98); frontend catch detects (FrameworksManager line 198)

title: No evidence/coverage impact preview before framework deactivation
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworksManager.jsx — deactivation confirmation modal body

Root Cause: The deactivation modal renders a static warning string. Before showing the modal, no API call is made to fetch: (a) the number of controls that will stop being tracked, (b) the number of evidence items mapped exclusively to controls in this framework, or (c) whether any active audit engagements reference this framework. The fw.controlCount is available from the prop but not displayed in the modal body.

Claude Fix Prompt: In FrameworksManager.jsx, update the deactivation confirmation modal to include a summary panel before the warning text:
```jsx
<Box bg="orange.50" borderRadius="md" p={3} mb={3}>
  <Text fontSize="sm" fontWeight="600">Impact Summary</Text>
  <Text fontSize="sm">{pendingMove?.controlCount ?? 0} controls will no longer be tracked</Text>
  <Text fontSize="sm">Coverage data for this framework will be removed from PCL on next sync</Text>
</Box>
```
This uses pendingMove.controlCount already available in state. For evidence impact, add a lightweight GET /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/frameworks/:frameworkId/impact endpoint that returns { controlCount, evidenceMappingCount } and fetch it when the modal opens.
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — orange impact Box in deactivation modal (FrameworksManager lines 586–596); controlCount shown

title: Control detail drawer has no navigation to evidence or policy items
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx — ControlDetailDrawer component, evidence/policy list rendering

Root Cause: Evidence items, policies, vendors, certifications, and integration items in the control drawer are rendered as plain <Text> or <Tag> elements. The evidence objects contain evidenceId (EV-uuid format) and the policy objects contain policyId, which are sufficient to construct navigation links to /evidence-management?id={evidenceId} and /policy-management?id={policyId}. These links are not implemented, making the compliance map a read-only dead-end.

Claude Fix Prompt: In FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx inside ControlDetailDrawer, wrap each evidence item title in a <Button variant="link" size="xs" onClick={() => router.push('/evidence-management')} rightIcon={<Icon as={ExternalLink} boxSize={3} />}> (or similar). For policies, navigate to /policy-management. For vendors, navigate to /vendors. Use useRouter from next/navigation (already imported). Add ExternalLink to the lucide-react import list.
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — evidence Button+ExternalLink (FrameworkComplianceMap lines 377–389); policy Button (lines 418–425)

title: CSV export missing PCL timestamp and six dimension score columns
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx — exportCSV() function, header row definition

Root Cause: The exportCSV function builds a header row with 12 columns. It does not include: pclSnapshotDate (available from data.lastSyncedAt), evidenceScore, policyScore, certScore, cloudScore, integrationScore, vendorScore (all available from ctrl.scores within each control object), integrationVerdict counts, or cloudPassCount/cloudFailCount. Auditors exporting for SoA evidence packaging need dimension scores to justify coverage claims.

Claude Fix Prompt: In FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx, update exportCSV():
1. Add pclSnapshotDate as a parameter (pass data?.lastSyncedAt).
2. Update the header row to add: 'PCL Snapshot Date', 'Evidence Score', 'Policy Score', 'Cert Score', 'Cloud Score', 'Integration Score', 'Vendor Score', 'Cloud Pass', 'Cloud Fail'.
3. In the data rows, add: new Date(pclSnapshotDate).toLocaleDateString(), ctrl.scores?.evidence ?? 0, ctrl.scores?.policy ?? 0, ctrl.scores?.cert ?? 0, ctrl.scores?.cloud ?? 0, ctrl.scores?.integration ?? 0, ctrl.scores?.vendor ?? 0, ctrl.cloud.reduce((s,c) => s + (c.passCount??0), 0), ctrl.cloud.reduce((s,c) => s + (c.failCount??0), 0).
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — 21-column header confirmed (lines 62–70); 6 dimension scores + cloud pass/fail + PCL date present

title: `availableFrameworks` hardcoded at limit=200 — silently drops frameworks
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/services/cfrsService.js (or compliance-frameworks.controller.js) — catalog fetch with limit=200

Root Cause: The catalog query fetches all frameworks with a hardcoded limit of 200. As the Vibrantix catalog grows (regional frameworks for APAC, GCC, EU added over time), orgs in those regions will not see all applicable frameworks in the browser. The API returns no totalCount or hasMore field in the getFrameworks response that the frontend could use to warn users.

Claude Fix Prompt:
1. In compliance-frameworks.controller.js getFrameworks(): Return { frameworks: [...], totalCount, page, limit } so callers can detect truncation.
2. In cfrsService.js: If totalCount > frameworks.length, log a console warning and surface a banner in FrameworksManager: "Showing {count} of {totalCount} available frameworks. Contact support to access the full catalog.".
3. As a short-term fix, raise the hardcoded limit to 500 until proper pagination is implemented.
